simulation.organization_and_actor: medium or large Brazilian discrete or process manufacturer; process engineer, quality engineer, and production supervisor
processes: detect process drift before scrap or rework rises
identify supplier or material shifts that change the operating envelope
triage abnormal production batches during peak or degraded operation
simulation.deterministic_baseline: SPC control charts, engineering limits, recipe and product-version controls, 4M change records, alarm rules, sampling, and human root-cause review
simulation.remaining_gap: Unsupervised drift detection may surface multivariate changes not covered by fixed limits, but the gap is not sufficiently distinct from existing equipment-condition monitoring and quality analytics once product, machine, material, and method context is modeled.

training_data.observation_unit: versioned production window or batch under one defined operating context
training_data.input_data: sensor and process variables available during production plus product, recipe, equipment, material-lot, shift, and 4M change context
training_data.target_or_reward: no mandatory target for unsupervised training; later quality result and engineer disposition used for evaluation and semi-supervised refinement
training_data.label_source: quality release, scrap or rework result, maintenance findings, and engineer-confirmed false or true alert
training_data.prediction_time: during or immediately after the production window, before final quality disposition where possible
training_data.expected_volume: unknown until a plant and line are selected
training_data.class_balance: abnormal events expected to be rare and heterogeneous; exact balance unknown
training_data.historical_coverage: requires versioned history spanning normal operation, product mix, planned changes, maintenance states, and seasonal or shift variation
training_data.train_validation_split: time-ordered and grouped by product, line, and change period; avoid random row splits
training_data.leakage_risks: final quality fields, rework codes, maintenance actions, or operator annotations created after alert time
training_data.representativeness_risks: new product variants, equipment changes, supplier lots, recipes, shifts, and maintenance states can change the normal envelope
training_data.feedback_loop: quality and process engineers confirm alert relevance and record legitimate 4M changes
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: worker or shift identifiers should be minimized and not used for individual performance profiling
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use SPC, engineering thresholds, versioned rules, targeted sampling, and a data-quality pilot before model training

portfolio_coherence.material_differentiation: not sufficient for a new opportunity; process-drift monitoring is best treated as an extension or experiment within existing manufacturing monitoring and quality workflows

evidence.role: concept drift and false-detection risk after 4M changes
technical plausibility and benchmarking limits for high-dimensional process drift
current Azure service lifecycle; Anomaly Detector retires on 2026-10-01

notes: No opportunity published. The selected lens exposed a plausible process-drift experiment, but deterministic SPC and versioned 4M context are strong baselines, false alerts under legitimate change are material, and the candidate overlaps the repository's existing manufacturing condition-monitoring pattern.
